name: Himatsingka Seide Ltd
title: Himatsingka Seide Ltd - 514043 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Home-textile maker pivoting to yarn, fabric and apparel verticals while Sheeting utilisation sits at 52% and revenue fell to INR634 crores from INR661 crores; no numeric guidance, so the read is a transition with volatility ahead.

summary.headline: Himatsingka Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell to INR634 crores from INR661 crores, with EBITDA of INR101 crores (~16% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated total income was INR634 crores against INR661 crores, described as range-bound, with shipment deferrals linked to Middle East geopolitical issues and lower capacity utilisation in some divisions. EBITDA came in at INR101 crores, a margin of about 16%, attributed to lower revenue, product mix tweaks and raw material inflation. Management said the call was mainly about the strategic transition to a multi-vertical model using existing assets: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions have started and are ramping up, Apparel Solutions is due a couple of quarters out, and Home Textiles (especially Sheeting) will be rightsized. Net leverage was described as range-bound at about INR2,550 crores.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR661 crores (prior period as stated; decline)
pressured by lower revenue, product mix and raw material inflation
purpose: debt tenor and maturity balancing

segments.name: Home Textile Solutions - Sheeting
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 52% in Q1; revenue expected to taper as capacity is rightsized and reallocated to new verticals.

segments.name: Home Textile Solutions - Terry
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 63%, unchanged from last quarter; management expects Terry to continue growing.

segments.name: Yarn Solutions
segments.commentary: Spinning assets (211,584 spindles, described as world's largest single-roof plant) being converted from captive to independent business; over 90% of capacity to be sold externally. Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores.

segments.name: Fabric Solutions
segments.commentary: Uses shared sheeting and knit processing capacity of about 90 million meters by year-end (vs 61 million meters earlier for home textiles, excluding knit). Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores; revenue generation has started.

segments.name: Apparel Solutions
segments.commentary: Planned for Phase 2, expected to launch a couple of quarters later; no revenue contribution discussed yet.

guidance_outlook: Transition period of a couple of quarters with expected volatility in numbers before new platforms stabilise.
Management aims to keep revenues range-bound with new verticals offsetting Sheeting decline, but expects Home Textile Solutions revenue to correct somewhat.
Net debt expected to reduce by end of fiscal year; leverage to stay range-bound.
Overall company expected to be transformed in about a year; India may become the largest or top-2 jurisdiction in the medium term.
Capex limited to maintenance and organic requirements; no expansion capex planned.
capex_capacity: Overall utilisation at facilities at 99% (as stated), with Sheeting at 52% and Terry at 63%.
Combined sheeting and knit fabric processing capacity to reach about 90 million meters by year-end, shared between Home Textile and Fabric Solutions.
Yarn spinning capacity of 211,584 spindles; majority to be sold externally.
Capex restricted to maintenance and organic needs; transition uses existing campus and infrastructure.
Apparel Solutions to start in Phase 2 using existing assets, a couple of quarters out.
demand_pricing: US demand affected by policy flip-flops and tariffs, creating inflationary pressure on products; management says tariff situation has stabilised at current levels.
Management expects pricing challenges in home textiles, especially Sheeting, and sees better pricing power in new verticals.
Shipment deferrals in the quarter linked to Middle East geopolitical issues.
UK FTA expected to help in medium term; EU FTA timing uncertain but expected in short term; still under process.
Management cited US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration as reasons for the pivot.

qa_highlights.question: What are the positives and negatives this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Negatives were revenue and offtake overhangs; positive is the start of the transition to the new multi-vertical model, which needs no expansion or capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise so much debt and how do tariffs affect the US business?
qa_highlights.answer: The recent NCD raise balances debt tenors and maturities and is not incremental capital. US tariff policy flip-flops created inflation and altered demand; tariff outlook has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: How will fabric capacity of 90 million meters be used versus the 61 million meters home capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The 61 million meters excluded knit platforms; combined 90 million meters will be allocated between Home Textile Sheeting and Fabric Solutions from common infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: How much yarn capacity will be sold externally and is more capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 90% of yarn capacity to be sold externally; capex kept to maintenance and organic needs only.

qa_highlights.question: Will lost Home Textile revenue be replaced in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for range-bound revenue, but Sheeting will be rightsized; Yarn and Fabric each target about INR1,000 crores at full capacity (about INR2,000 crores combined), with no quarterly split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Sheeting ramp-down about profitability or US challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration led to repositioning the business as Himatsingka 2.0.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility during transition: management warned of volatility over the next couple of quarters.
Sheeting rightsizing and pricing pressure in home textiles, especially US, with utilisation at 52%.
Ramp-up execution of Yarn and Fabric Solutions, with no quarterly revenue split disclosed.
Raw material inflation and margin pressure (EBITDA margin ~16%).
Timing of UK and EU FTAs and Apparel Solutions launch; equity initiatives to be shared later without details.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term strategic direction but cautious near term, repeatedly flagging volatility and transition for a couple of quarters. Evasive on quarterly vertical revenue split and on the timing and size of equity initiatives.
key_quotes: So our efforts are essentially geared to transforming the Himatsingka model and steering away from U.S. concentration, steering away from client concentration, as we've seen in the Home Textile space, that seems to be a cornerstone of the home textile, let's say, world.
We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.
So therefore, all in all, we will see a reduction in net debt by the end of fiscal.
